source_name: ECB Data Portal — PSS: Payments and Settlement Systems Statistics (DISCONTINUED, API-only)
why_relevant: The retired predecessor of the current ECB payment statistics, covering access/usage of payment services and terminals, TARGET2 per country and national retail systems, with Slovakia included. Explicitly not exposed in the portal UI and reachable only through the API — a textbook retired-series surface for a continuity cell, giving pre-methodology-break history that the current datasets no longer carry.

source_name: Legacy ECB Statistical Data Warehouse (sdw.ecb.europa.eu) — Slovakia payments country tables
why_relevant: The retired SDW front-end (superseded by data.ecb.europa.eu) still surfaces in indexes with a Slovakia payments country-table node. Useful as a legacy-identifier map (old node/series keys → new dataset keys) and as a Wayback target where the old tables were laid out differently.

source_name: Štatistický úrad SR — DATAcube./STATdata public database API (data.statistics.sk/api/v2)
why_relevant: Fully documented public REST API over the Slovak statistical office's multidimensional cubes, returning JSON-stat/CSV/XML/XLSX/ODS. Provides household finance, retail turnover and ICT/e-commerce context series for cash-vs-card behaviour, and a collection endpoint that enumerates every available cube — including ones being migrated or retired.

source_name: DATAcube → STATdata migration (dual-running legacy and successor SK statistical databases)
why_relevant: ŠÚ SR is migrating the whole DATAcube database into a new STATdata platform, with new cubes created only in the new system while both run in parallel. This is an active continuity risk and opportunity: cube identifiers and URLs will change, and the legacy database is the vintage of record until it is switched off.

source_name: Open Data MF SR (opendata.mfsr.sk) — Ministry of Finance open data portal
why_relevant: Ministry of Finance machine-readable datasets (public finance, budget, state institution payments). Indirect but durable context for cashless-transition policy and for public-sector payment volumes; a second publisher whose retired datasets are catalogued alongside NBS in data.gov.sk.

source_name: IMF Financial Access Survey (FAS) — SDMX API, ATM/POS/branch indicators for Slovakia
why_relevant: Annual, internationally comparable ATM, POS/agent-outlet and account-usage indicators for Slovakia going back to the mid-2000s, exposed via SDMX 2.1/3.0 with no authentication. Independent of NBS web structure, so it preserves long history when national pages break.

source_name: World Bank Open Data / FRED mirrors of Slovak ATM-density indicators
why_relevant: Re-publication of IMF FAS ATM indicators for Slovakia with a stable indicator code and a well-documented bulk API; FRED (e.g. SVKFCAKNUM) offers a second mirror with its own vintage/ALFRED revision history — valuable when the primary source revises silently.

source_name: BIS Data Portal — CPMI payments and FMI (Red Book) statistics, bulk CSV/SDMX
why_relevant: Since Dec 2023 the Red Book payment statistics are disseminated through the BIS Data Portal with zipped CSV and SDMX bulk files and comparative tables on cards, terminals, cashless payments and cash withdrawals. Slovakia is NOT a CPMI member jurisdiction, so treat this as a comparator/benchmark surface rather than a source of SK data — still valuable for methodology definitions (CPMI d168) that NBS-era series were aligned to.

source_name: Archív Národnej banky Slovenska (archiv.nbs.sk) — institutional/physical archive and research portal
why_relevant: Statutory archive (act 395/2002) holding 200+ archival fonds from defunct monetary institutions and the Czechoslovak State Bank, with a bádateľský portál (researcher portal). Not a source of modern payment statistics — inspection showed no statistics sections — but the correct route for pre-digital and long-retired NBS records and for formal document requests.

source_name: CRZP — Centrálny register záverečných prác (Slovak central theses repository, CVTI SR)
why_relevant: National repository of all Slovak bachelor/master/doctoral and habilitation theses, retained 70 years. Theses on Slovak card usage, ATM networks and cash demand routinely reproduce NBS tables and bank-supplied figures for years whose original online sources are gone — a genuine long-tail recovery surface for retired series.

source_name: NBS SDDS Plus / national summary data page (data categories with published release calendar)
why_relevant: SDDS Plus obliges NBS to publish defined data categories on a fixed, machine-readable release calendar with stable landing pages — an unusually stable anchor for automated ingestion and for detecting when a category is redefined or discontinued.

source_name: NBS 'Subjekty finančného trhu' register with bulk download (hromadné sťahovanie údajov)
why_relevant: NBS announced bulk download for its financial market entities database — a machine-readable register of banks, payment institutions and e-money institutions. Repeated snapshots give an entry/exit time series for the SK payments market that no published statistic provides.

source_name: NBS 'PTK – Open Data' procurement / preliminary market consultation documents
why_relevant: NBS procurement documents for an Open Data solution (data catalogue, data repository, presentation layer, API). These reveal the intended architecture, planned endpoints and dataset scope of NBS open data before it goes live — an early-warning pointer to future machine-readable NBS surfaces.

source_name: Slovenská banková asociácia (SBA) — publications and member-data statistics
why_relevant: Industry association covering 23 members / >99% of the Slovak banking sector; its analyses and reports are the source layer behind NBS card issuing and acquiring statistics (which are compiled from SBA member data). Historic SBA publications sometimes carry sector series that NBS never published separately.

source_name: ECB Data Portal — Payments statistics data category (PSS / payment services, LVPS and retail payment systems)
why_relevant: Harmonised semi-annual payment statistics collected under Regulation ECB/2020/59, with SK country rows: number of cards, card payments, terminals, credit transfers, direct debits, e-money. Longer-run and more comparable than NBS national tables.

source_name: ECB Data Portal — Payment card accepting devices (ATM / POS terminal counts)
why_relevant: The single most directly on-topic ECB cut for Printec-type interests: counts of ATMs, POS terminals and e-money card accepting devices per country, including Slovakia — terminal estate size and growth over time.

source_name: ECB Data Portal — Cards and card payments key figures
why_relevant: Curated headline indicators (cards per capita, transactions per card, average value) with country comparison views; fast way to benchmark Slovakia against euro-area peers without building series keys.

source_name: ECB Payments statistics press releases (semi-annual, H1/H2)
why_relevant: Narrative + chart release accompanying each semi-annual payment statistics vintage; gives the official reading of trends (card share, contactless, fraud, terminals) and flags methodological breaks that matter when splicing SK series.

source_name: ECB SPACE — Study on the payment attitudes of consumers in the euro area (landing page)
why_relevant: The flagship Eurosystem consumer payment-diary survey (2020, 2022, 2024 waves) with per-country results including Slovakia: cash share at POS, P2P cash use, stated preferences, cash access perceptions. Only harmonised demand-side cash-usage evidence for SK.

source_name: ECB SPACE 2024 — Annex B (country-level statistical annex)
why_relevant: The annexes carry the machine-extractable per-country tables (SK rows) behind the SPACE headline text — cash/card/mobile shares by transaction value band, location, and payment situation. This is where the usable Slovakia numbers actually live.

source_name: ECB SPACE 2020 report (first wave, baseline)
why_relevant: Baseline wave (2019 diary fieldwork, 17 euro area countries incl. Slovakia) needed to measure the SK cash-to-card shift over time rather than reading a single snapshot.

source_name: ECB Occasional Paper 201 — The use of cash by households in the euro area
why_relevant: The pre-SPACE (SUCH 2016) study establishing the long-run cash-usage baseline per country, incl. Slovakia; essential for a 2016→2024 cash decline narrative and for understanding the methodology lineage of SPACE.

source_name: Joint EBA–ECB Report on Payment Fraud (annual, country breakdowns)
why_relevant: Successor to the ECB card fraud report series; semi-annual fraud data by instrument (cards, credit transfers, cash withdrawals, e-money) with per-country tables covering Slovakia. Directly relevant to ATM/POS fraud and SCA effects.

source_name: ECB Seventh report on card fraud (legacy card-fraud series)
why_relevant: The discontinued ECB card fraud report series (through 2021) carrying CNP vs ATM vs POS fraud splits by country, incl. SK; needed for back-history before the EBA-ECB joint series began.

source_name: ECB SDMX 2.1 RESTful web service (ECB Data Portal API)
why_relevant: The machine-readable access layer for every SK payment/card/terminal series above — XML/JSON/CSV, data-discovery endpoints, and bulk download for datasets not exposed in the web UI. This is the recommended collection channel for the whole cell.

source_name: ECB Data Portal — Payments statistics methodology page
why_relevant: Explains definitions, breaks in series, derogations and the reporting manual behind the SK rows. Without it, cross-country ATM/POS comparisons are easy to misread (e.g. terminal definitions, MCC breakdowns, resident vs non-resident acquiring).

source_name: Regulation (EU) 2020/2011 (ECB/2020/59) on payments statistics — EUR-Lex
why_relevant: The legal instrument that forces Slovak PSPs to report card, terminal and fraud data to NBS and thence to the ECB. Reading the annexes tells you exactly which variables exist for SK before you go looking for them, and is available in Slovak on EUR-Lex.

source_name: ECB public consultation file on the payments statistics Regulation (FAQ + draft annexes)
why_relevant: Consultation FAQs and draft annexes reveal the reporting burden debate and the exact variable list (MCC breakdowns, remote/contactless, fraud typologies) — useful for anticipating which SK series will appear and which are derogated.

source_name: ECB TARGET Services Annual Report (TIPS / T2 country contributions)
why_relevant: Reports per-country shares of instant payment volumes settled in TIPS; the 2024 edition explicitly names Slovakia as one of the three largest contributors of euro instant payments — a high-signal, hard-to-source fact about the SK instant-payments market.
